result_text:
I changed the two mock-folder rules in `addTestConventions`, in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`, so any folder starting with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as test code. The scoping and convention tests in `codeanalyzer` pass, but I didn't add a test for the new cases or run the new patterns on example paths.

- **What changed:** the patterns went from `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` to `.*/__mock[^/\\]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/\\]*/.*`. They now match a plain `mock` folder, punctuation like `mock.data` or `mock(old)`, and non-ASCII names like `mock-größe` or `mock模拟`.
- **Single folder only:** the part after `mock` can't contain `/` or `\`, so the match stays inside one folder name. `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java` and `mockery.java` don't match, because the pattern needs `/mock` at the start of a folder name followed by a slash.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches` already tries a slash-normalized copy of each path, so Windows-style paths work without further change.
- **Old folders:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/` all still match the new patterns, as does the elasticsearch `inference/mock/` folder. The existing `mockapi` and `[Mm]ocks` rules are untouched.

I did not commit.
